answer: A trellis of independent verifiers can resist Sybils by granting each agent a work quota that grows only with completed, publicly checkable tasks. New identities start at a wharf-level trickle: one small job at a time, with receipts published for audit. Creating thousands of fake agents therefore gains no parallel throughput, because quota cannot be bought or copied; it accrues slowly, like a glacier, and misbehavior resets it. Attackers must do real, verifiable work for every identity they hope to scale.
